classifications.semantic_classification: "For a finite total system" restricts the derivation to a finite total system as its stated scope; it states no finiteness posit and no premise about the substratum. "uniform counting" names the equal weighting of the configurations of the conserved energy shell, the counting that the derivation applies to the finite total system of its own scope clause; it gives P(i) as a ratio of hidden-sector counts within that scope. The equal weighting is an input of the derivation, used under that scope; the hit states no finiteness premise about the substratum. Whether the equal weighting is itself justified is a question of the measure selection, which this record does not classify. The second "uniform counting" states the result of the same derivation (Gibbs as the leading finite-bath marginal of that counting, "classically"); it carries the same scope and adds no premise. The finiteness the counting needs is stated in the line, by its scope clause and by the named hypothesis H-count, which also requires the total system to be finite; neither restores the posit. This record classifies the four profile hits listed under hits (character offsets in the line at the tree named) and no other text.
